page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this arm64 platform features 768 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, without any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 11099.56 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 218.19 GB/sec. Database operations are a key strength, as evidenced by top-tier Passmark database scores and Redis SET performance of 201.15 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the average and strong tiers respectively.

Tradeoffs are visible in specific workloads; while LLM text generation for medium and large models ranks as strong, text generation for small 135M models falls into the bottom 10% tier. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dense local NVMe storage make this bare-metal instance highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive, I/O-heavy workloads without the overhead of virtualization. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, caching layers, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
